# Impact numbers (generated by src/impact.py, do not edit by hand)

Representative weekday: Wednesday 2026-02-11 (RTS Spring 2026 GTFS). A bus visit is one scheduled bus arrival at a stop.

## Sentences you can use

- On a typical weekday RTS makes 39,703 bus visits to 971 stops. 44 percent of them fall between 11 am and 5 pm, the hottest part of the day, when our morning satellite data understates the heat.
- 49 percent of weekday bus visits are at stops OpenStreetMap lists as having no shelter, and another 28 percent are at stops with unknown shelter status. Only 23 percent are at stops it lists as sheltered.
- The 20 highest-priority stops get 3,355 bus visits a weekday, 8 percent of the system total, from 2 percent of stops. 47 percent of those visits are in the 11 am to 5 pm window.
- The 20 stops that most lack shade (Stream A's shade-need list) get 998 bus visits a weekday. Only 4 stops appear on both top 20 lists, so the two lists point to different places.

| Measure | Value |

| Stops in the data | 971 |

| Of which 11 am to 5 pm | 17,453 (44.0 percent) |

| Visits at the shade-need top 20 | 998 (2.5 percent) |

## Read these with the limits

- A bus visit is not a rider. It is the best public proxy for how many people wait.
- Shelter shares depend on OpenStreetMap, which is partial. Unknown is not the same as none.
- The schedule is the Spring 2026 feed and one representative Wednesday.
- Afternoon here means scheduled bus times, not measured afternoon temperatures.
